body: Yeah, I'm planning to (and I believe am expected to) take a closer look at this. Given that 4.4-beta1 (and its feature freeze) is just around the corner I would imagine that something as big as this is better suited for after 4.4-stable though.

I'll do a more in-depth review of the code/design at some later point, but I think this feature could be a good candidate for something like the server-specific properties discussed [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/10438#issuecomment-2306922209), rather than tacking on stuff to the shared `PhysicsServer3D` interface that can't (?) be implemented by both physics engines (and perhaps also current/future physics extensions).

Merging this as-is would (in my opinion) set the somewhat unfortunate precedent of adding "Jolt-only" stuff to the shared `PhysicsServer3D` interface. If anything, we should aim to deprecate and move things away from the shared interface, to instead be provided per-server, for things that aren't deemed widely applicable to all/most other physics engines out there.

From just a quick look, I am seeing per-shape materials supported by PhysX, Havok (judging by the Unity Physics and Babylon.js APIs), Rapier, bepuphysics, Newton and ODE, but not Bullet, so perhaps this concept is leaning more towards widely applicable either way, but with the Jolt module currently being considered experimental, and Godot Physics being the default 3D physics engine for the foreseeable future (theoretically forever) it would still seem unfortunate to expose this through `PhysicsServer3D`.

Exposing this through `PhysicsServer3D` also raises the question why this isn't exposed in `PhysicsServer2D`, even if just as an empty implementation.

With all that said, we obviously don't have the above mentioned per-server property functionality at the moment, which puts this PR in a weird limbo, but I'm hoping we can have it added in some basic form shortly after 4.4-stable is out.
Wouldn't the best option be to implement per-shape materials in Godot Physics, to match most physics engines? I don't know how much of a lift that would be.

Sure, if that's added to this PR, then it's a different story, but I also don't know what's involved with adding per-shape materials to Godot Physics, nor what the consequences of adding that might be.

From just a quick look, it would seem to me like the shape information is available in the places where bounce and friction are being combined (`GodotBodyPair*D::pre_solve` and `GodotBodyPair*D::solve` respectively) but more than that I can't really say.
